title: fix(react): one Ctrl+Z pops one undo, however many useGlobalUndo instances are mounted, and a focused field keeps its own undo (objectui#11081)
body:
Fixes #11081
Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

Every mounted `useGlobalUndo` added its own `window` `keydown` listener, and each one popped the one shared `globalUndoManager`. The console mounts several instances at once, so one Ctrl+Z reverted one saved record write per mounted instance, as many as were stacked. The handler also never read the event target: Ctrl+Z typed into a text field was `preventDefault`ed, the field's own undo did not run, and the last saved record write was reverted instead.

## What changes (`packages/react/src/hooks/useGlobalUndo.ts` only)

- **Exactly one listener.** Each instance registers its options ref in a module-level, insertion-ordered `Set`. The first registration adds the one module-level `keydown` handler; the last unregistration removes it. The registration effect runs once per mount and is keyed on the ref, whose identity React keeps, not on a memoised `undo` / `redo` (AGENTS.md rule 10), so an instance's place in the keyboard order is its mount order.
- **One keypress pops at most one operation** (`popUndo`, or `popRedo` with Shift), and exactly one instance answers it: its `dataSource` runs the write and its `onUndo` / `onRedo` fires.
- **No interception in an editable target.** When the target is an `input`, `textarea`, `select` or contenteditable region (`isContentEditable`, which also covers a node nested inside one), the handler returns before `preventDefault` and before any pop, so the browser's own undo runs in the field.
- **Unchanged:** the hook's signature, `UseGlobalUndoOptions`, the return shape, and the returned `undo` / `redo` (what a toast's Undo button calls), which still run through the instance they belong to. The hook's emitted declaration was compared at base and head: the only difference is the added JSDoc paragraph.

## Which instance answers a keypress: the longest-mounted live one

Measured at `origin/main` `3e71a9825`: an `UndoableOperation` carries `id`, `type`, `objectName`, `recordId`, `timestamp`, `description`, `undoData` and `redoData`, and nothing that names the instance whose runner pushed it. The push happens in `@object-ui/core`'s `ActionRunner` (`globalUndoManager.push(result.undo)`), outside the hook module. An owner field would change an exported core type and the runner, which the claim puts out of scope. So the rule is the dispatch's fallback: the first entry of the set, which is the longest-mounted live instance. When it unmounts, the next-oldest takes over.

That is also the instance that already answered whenever a single operation was stacked. Its listener was first on `window` and popped the operation, and the rest found the stack empty; the card's probe measured exactly that. So a single-operation Ctrl+Z behaves as before, and only the extra pops are gone. The choice is written in the hook's JSDoc and in the block comment above the registry.

## Pins: `useGlobalUndo.oneListener-11081.test.tsx`

Real hook, real `globalUndoManager`, real `keydown` events that bubble to `window`.

- Three instances, three operations: one Ctrl+Z pops exactly one (one `dataSource.delete`, one `onUndo`, `defaultPrevented` true).
- Ctrl+Shift+Z with three instances and three redoable operations pops exactly one redo.
- The longest-mounted instance answers. After it unmounts, its successor answers. An instance mounted by a later commit does not.
- Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z in a focused `input`, `textarea`, `select`, contenteditable region, and a node nested inside one (five cases): the stack is untouched, `defaultPrevented` is false, and no callback runs. A focused `button` still pops (the control).
- Three instances add one `keydown` listener. Unmounting all of them removes that same function, and a later keypress pops nothing and is not `defaultPrevented`.
- StrictMode double-mount: one pop per keypress, `keydown` adds and removes balance after unmount, and nothing pops afterwards.
- A toast-style `undo()` on an instance that does not own the keyboard runs that instance's `dataSource` and `onUndo`, not the keyboard owner's.

## Evidence (all at head `f89bd44d4`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/react/` plus the three tests that drive a real consumer's undo (`useConsoleActionRuntime.undoneToast-11056.test.tsx`, `RecordDetailView.undoneToast-11056.test.tsx`, `undoProjectedRow-10404.test.tsx`): `Test Files 107 passed (107)`, `Tests 1377 passed (1377)`, that is 104 react files plus 3.
- Reverse verification, after committing the fix: the hook file was replaced by its `3e71a9825` blob (on-disk proof: blob equal to the base blob, `onUndoShortcut` count 3 to 0), then the new and existing pins ran: `Tests 10 failed | 6 passed (16)`. Red: the three one-pop pins, the five editable-target pins and the two lifecycle pins. Green at base, as expected: the button control, the toast-style `undo()` pin and the four existing option-timing pins. Restored with `git checkout HEAD`: blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- Guard ablation through `ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor `if (isEditableTarget(e.target)) return;` count 1 to 0, blob moved): exactly the five editable-target pins went red, `Tests 5 failed | 7 passed (12)`. Restored: blob equal to HEAD.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/react type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0, after building the dependency closure with `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/react^...' build`. The test tsconfig's `--listFiles` includes the new pin file.
- `check-changeset-presence`, `check-control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:self-import` and `check:phantom-deps` all exit 0. `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on the three paths answers NOT GOVERNED.

**Declared narrowing.** `pnpm lint` and the full `pnpm test` run are CI's. ESLint ran on the two changed source files only. The population is those two files: ESLint linted both and ignored neither. The count, 2 files with 0 errors and 0 warnings, is read from `--format json`. `eslint.config.js` declares no type-aware linting (no `projectService`, `parserOptions` or `TypeChecked` config), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file. The app-shell `AppContent.*` tests that stub `useGlobalUndo` were not run, because they replace the hook and cannot see this change.

**Not measured:** a browser run of the console. Which instance is the oldest on a given route is read from source, not measured.

## Acceptance notes

- A keyboard undo runs the write through the answering instance's `dataSource`. An instance without one pops without reverting. That behavior is unchanged: it is what the first-registered listener did before. In the console, all three call sites pass the same adapter (read from source).
- For the operation's owner to answer the keypress, `UndoableOperation` would need an owner and the `ActionRunner` push would have to set it. That is a core contract change, and it is not proposed here.

Changeset: `.changeset/11081-one-undo-listener.md`, `'@object-ui/react': patch`.
